Labeed was a hypocrite belonging to the Banu Zurayq tribe and was an ally to the Jews. The angel enquired further, 'Upon what did he carry it out?' 'Upon a comb and the hairs it had removed,' the other replied. 'Where is it now?' was the next question. The reply was, 'In the male spathe of a palm beneath a rock in the Dharwaan well.'"
Rasulullaah ﷺ then went to the well and had the thing removed. Rasulullaah ﷺ also said, "This was the very well I was shown with water appearing like that used to wash a henna-filled container and the palms of which appeared to be the heads of the Shayaateen." Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) asked, "Why did you not publicise the event?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Allaah had cured me from it and I do not wish to start a scandal against someone."[^1]

Another narration adds that Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "It was for six months that Rasulullaah ﷺ would think that he had been to his wives when in reality he had not. Two angels then came to him..." The rest of the Hadith continues (like the one above).[^2]
Rasulullaah ﷺ Shows Tolerance Towards the Jewish Woman who Served him Poisoned Meat

Hadhrat Anas (RA) reports that a Jewish woman once gave Rasulullaah ﷺ a poisoned goat meat, which he ate from. When the woman was later brought before Rasulullaah ﷺ (when he discovered what she had done), he questioned her about it. "I wanted to kill you," she admitted. Rasulullaah ﷺ responded by saying, "Allaah would never give the power to kill me." "Are you not going to have her executed?" the Sahabah (RA) asked. "No," replied Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "I could always notice the effect of the poison on Rasulullaah ﷺ's uvula."[^3]

Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrates that a Jewish woman once presented some goat meat to Rasulullaah ﷺ which was poisoned. "Hang on," Rasulullaah ﷺ cautioned the Sahabah (RA), "this is poisoned." Rasulullaah ﷺ then questioned the woman, "What made you do this?" Her response was, "I wanted to know that if you really are a Rasul, Allaah would inform you about it and if you are not, people could be rid of you." Rasulullaah ﷺ did not take any action against her.[^4]

Another narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) adds that whenever Rasulullaah ﷺ felt the effect of the poison, he would have his blood cupped. In fact, when he was on a journey and about to enter the state of Ihraam on one occasion, he sensed its effect and had cupping done.[^5]
